key_insight: Similarity-based positional encoding (simPE) is not rotation-invariant, but it is provably stable under small rotational perturbations and performs better than standard learned positional encoding in rotated image settings.
clinical_relevance: For medical imaging models that may encounter slight patient or acquisition-related rotations, simPE may improve robustness without sacrificing positional structure.
method: Theoretical analysis of simPE under rotations with Lipschitz-based perturbation bounds.
Experimental comparison on synthetic Arrow, Shapes, Digits, and FashionMNIST datasets.
Test images were rotated while training/validation images stayed in canonical orientation.
evidence_signal: Across four datasets, simPE outperformed learned positional encoding on accuracy, F1, precision, and recall, especially at small-to-moderate rotation angles.
watch_item: Results come from controlled rotation experiments, so real-world medical imaging performance may depend on the architecture, rotation magnitude, and how well the positional encoding is implemented.
paper_title: Robustness of Similarity-based Positional Encoding Under Rotations: Theoretical Analysis and Experimental Validation
